I explained that he was in a lot of pain and fluid weeping from his ear.. I continued to explain we had been abroad and he had completed a course of antibiotics whilst away for a ear infection but this has come back. the lady I was speaking to was actually the practice manager. She told me there were no appointments and I would need to.call the out of hours number when the closed, 80 minutes later. It takes minutes to look in a ear and give a prescription!  Now as a minor they have a duty of care to see him .. but she was adamant that the doctor was too busy. I spoke to a few staff during the night on the 111 line who told me that the doctor should have seen him and how bad he had been treated by the practice manager. I am so annoyed that I wasn’t more persistent. As I worked in a gp surgery as a receptionist and was always told if under 16 we have a duty of care to add them to the list to see the doctor!

As I write this it is 4.30am and I’m still waiting for the actual doctor to call… he is crying in pain and unable to sleep!

After ordering my repeat prescription a week ago, I arrived to pick it up, but was sent away with no medication because I had ordered it too early.
This woman could have done more to help and easily found a solution.

Leaving in the morning to spend almost 2 months abroad (reason why ordered early) with no medicine to treat the severe asthma that I've suffered with all my life and the high blood pressure and Cholesterol that has been diagnosed recently in the past 6 months, I'm 50+ years old.

The doctors here and the health practitioner's are all lovely, they do a great job and have really helped me so much over the years, the receptionists have been good too, but this one will end causing serious harm if she is not retrained or continues to serve and behave in this manner.

I'm thinking to half the remaining medication so it will last longer, or not take it some days.
Hoping I will be able to get medication at my destination, it's not the right thing to do but what choice have I left.
